transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good morning, thank you for calling S-Net Fibre and Voice Support. My name is Owen speaking today. Who do I have on the line, please?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Owen, my name is Ferdinand Vance. I'm calling from my neighbour's house up the hill because my broadband and phone line are completely dead.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good morning, Ferdinand. Let me pull up your S-Net profile first. Could you give me your ten-digit account number and your date of birth, please?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the account number is 8849201734, and my date of birth is the fourteenth of November 1958.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, Ferdinand. I have account 8849201734 open on my screen now. Tell me what happened to your fibre broadband and telephone service this morning.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We had a violent thunderstorm across the valley around four o'clock this morning, with lightning striking right near our lane, and everything went off immediately.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, I see. When you went outside this morning, did you notice any physical damage to the overhead cable or the wooden telegraph pole?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, pole number DP-449 at the corner of Millbrook Lane has a split cross-arm, and the black overhead fibre cable is snapped and coiled by the hedge.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So to summarize, lightning from this morning's storm damaged pole DP-449 on Millbrook Lane and severed your overhead dropwire, leaving both your broadband and landline completely dead.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's right, and I am genuinely terrified because our isolated farm cottage is in a deep stone hollow with zero mobile signal indoors and no landline for emergencies.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have noted on the ticket that there is no indoor mobile reception at the cottage. Let's go through the mandatory safety and equipment checks first.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My wife has a heart condition and if she needs an ambulance overnight we have no way to ring out at all without walking half a mile uphill!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have recorded that medical note on the log, Ferdinand. First safety question for Openreach: is the snapped black cable hanging across a road where vehicles pass?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, the cable fell onto the grass verge on the inside of the hedgerow, so tractors and cars can still get past on the lane.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good. Second safety question: is that telegraph pole carrying any mains electricity power cables, or is there any sparking or charring near the base?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, it's purely a telecommunications pole with the yellow warning band on it, no electrical transformers or power lines attached to it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And is the broken wooden cross-arm dangling loose where it could fall onto a pedestrian walking along Millbrook Lane, or is it lodged against the pole?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's hanging at an awkward angle held up by one rusty bolt, so if the wind picks up tonight it could easily drop onto the footpath.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That classifies it as a structural overhead hazard. Now let me check the equipment inside your cottage. Do you still have mains electricity inside the house?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the mains electricity flickered during the storm at four in the morning, but the fuse board stayed on and our sockets are working fine.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When you looked at the white Openreach optical network terminal box mounted on your interior wall, which indicator lights were illuminated or flashing?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The power light is solid green, the optical LOS light is flashing bright red, and the PON and LAN lights are completely dark.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: A flashing red LOS light confirms total loss of light through the external fibre strand, matching the severed dropwire outside at pole DP-449.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And the battery backup unit next to the white box has been letting out a loud piercing beep every thirty seconds since dawn.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Did you press the silence alarm button on the side of the Nokia battery backup unit before you walked up to your neighbour's house?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I held the little grey button down for five seconds and the beeping stopped, though the red fault LED on the battery pack stayed lit.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And on your S-Net Hub 5 router itself, where your cordless home telephone base station plugs into the green voice port, what colour was the front bar?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The front light bar on the S-Net Hub 5 is pulsing orange continuously, and when I pick up the landline handset there is no dial tone.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Did you also check whether any other cottages along Millbrook Lane are fed from that same pole DP-449, or is yours the only dropwire on it?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Ours is the only cottage down at the bottom of the hollow fed from pole DP-449; my neighbour Arthur up the hill is on a different line.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: All right, those hardware diagnostics give me everything required for the line telemetry report. Let me open the wholesale hazard dispatch form now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How quickly can you get an engineer out here with a cherry picker to restring the cable? We really cannot be cut off for days.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before the wholesale portal lets me submit the hazard form, I realized I only took your account number earlier and skipped full verification.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, did you? What else do you need from me to get the form through?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: To complete verification now, could you confirm your full property address including the postcode, and also your four-digit account PIN, Ferdinand?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Certainly, the property address is Brackenfell Cottage, Millbrook Lane, Hexham, Northumberland, NE46 2QT, and my four-digit PIN is 7391.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, Ferdinand. I have verified Brackenfell Cottage, NE46 2QT and your PIN 7391 on the system now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, now please tell me someone can come out today to fix pole DP-449 and reconnect our line.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am going to check the live Openreach hoist and hazard engineering schedule now. Please bear with me for a moment while I contact their dispatch desk.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: All right, I will wait on the line.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, Ferdinand. I have spoken with the Openreach regional hazard controller and logged the damaged cross-arm on pole DP-449.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What did they say? Are they sending a crew out to Millbrook Lane this afternoon?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because pole DP-449 has a damaged wooden cross-arm and requires a two-person overhead hoist vehicle and road safety signage, standard solo vans cannot climb it.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, so when does the two-person hoist vehicle arrive at Brackenfell Cottage?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: An emergency make-safe barrier technician will attend within four hours to secure the loose cross-arm, and the overhead hoist crew is booked for Friday morning in forty-eight hours.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Forty-eight hours?! Owen, I just told you my wife has a heart condition and we have no phone line or indoor mobile signal at all!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The hoist crew has twelve storm-damaged poles across Northumberland queued ahead of Millbrook Lane after last night's lightning strikes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Surely S-Net can escalate this as a vulnerable household priority so we aren't left cut off in the middle of nowhere for two whole days!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have already flagged the welfare indicator on Openreach hazard reference OR-992841-HX, which moved your hoist slot from next Tuesday forward to Friday morning.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Friday morning is still two nights without a working landline or broadband connection in our cottage because a pole snapped in the storm!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The hoist machinery and replacement timber cross-arm have to come from the Newcastle heavy plant depot, and Friday between eight and one is the earliest slot.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I pay S-Net sixty-two pounds every month for dependable fibre and Digital Voice, and the moment bad weather hits we are left completely isolated!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Well, Ferdinand, I obviously can't control the British weather or stop lightning hitting a pole, can I?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Excuse me? There is no need to take that sarcastic tone with me when I am worried sick about reaching an ambulance for my wife!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let's stick to the practical steps I can take for your connection while we wait for the Openreach hoist crew on Friday morning.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What practical steps can you possibly take if the fibre cable is lying in the hedge outside?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Although you mentioned having no indoor cellular signal, you said earlier that your attic gable window faces up the hill toward your neighbour's house.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, if you stand right up by the top attic window facing the ridge you can sometimes get one or two bars of 4G outdoors.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am taking personal ownership of ordering an S-Net 4G Always-Connected Backup Hub with a high-gain window suction antenna for you right now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How does that backup hub work, and how quickly would it actually get out to Hexham?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am dispatching it via pre-noon courier to your cottage for tomorrow morning, pre-activated with unlimited data at zero charge.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And if we mount the suction antenna on the attic window, will that let our cordless phone work downstairs?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, Ferdinand. You plug the 4G backup unit into the WAN port of your S-Net Hub 5, and your Digital Voice landline handset will work over 4G.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That would actually give us a working emergency phone inside the cottage tomorrow until the hoist crew repairs the pole on Friday.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly. I have generated the courier dispatch under order reference BK-440192 and linked it directly to your outage ticket so you won't be billed a penny.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you for arranging that backup unit, Owen. What happens if I need updates on the Openreach hoist crew since my mobile doesn't work indoors?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Since you are calling from your neighbour's telephone right now, would your neighbour mind if I add their landline number as a secondary contact on the ticket?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My neighbour Arthur said that is completely fine—his number is the 01434 number I am calling you from right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have added Arthur's 01434 landline as the primary voice contact for Openreach engineer pre-call alerts, and kept your mobile for SMS updates when you walk uphill.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will someone from Openreach need to come inside Brackenfell Cottage on Friday morning when they restring the overhead fibre cable?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, once the two-person hoist crew replaces the cross-arm on pole DP-449 and runs a new dropwire to your eaves, they will test light levels at your internal box.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I will make sure either my wife or I am home between eight o'clock and one o'clock on Friday morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have also enabled Ofcom automatic loss-of-service compensation on account 8849201734, which credits nine pounds and seventy-six pence per full day after forty-eight hours.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does that credit go onto my next monthly S-Net statement automatically once the fibre line is working again?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, Ferdinand, I have set a personal follow-up task in my queue for Friday afternoon at two o'clock to verify the optical signal and confirm the credit.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you read back the reference numbers so I can write them on my notepad before I walk back down the lane?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Of course. Your Openreach overhead hazard and hoist reference is OR-992841-HX, booked for Friday morning between 08:00 and 13:00.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Got that written down, OR-992841-HX. And what was the courier reference for the 4G backup hub and window antenna?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The pre-noon DPD courier order reference is BK-440192, arriving tomorrow before twelve midday at Brackenfell Cottage.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, I have both numbers written down. So my broadband and phone line are still completely off for now until the kit and engineers arrive.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Correct, your overhead fibre line remains down pending the Openreach hoist repair on Friday, with the 4G backup hub arriving tomorrow morning.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: All right, I will look out for the make-safe technician today and the courier tomorrow morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else I can check on your account today while I have you on the line, Ferdinand?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that's everything for now, thank you.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, Ferdinand, and there will be a brief survey after this call. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.
